newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Reliance Telecom to invest 30 bln rupees.
newsitem.headline: India's Reliance Telecom to invest 30 bln rupees.

text.p: India's Reliance Telecom Pvt Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to invest 30 billion rupees over the next few years in a project to provide basic telephone services in western Gujarat state.
The company signed the licence agreement with the federal government's department of telecommunications (DoT) to build and operate basic telephone services in Gujarat.
The licence is valid for 15 years and can be extended, for 10 years at a time, it said in a statement.
The licence also covers the union territories of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, it said.
Reliance Telecom is a joint venture of India's largest private firm Reliance Industries and Nynex International, part of Nynex Co of U.S.
The joint venture obtained the licence at an attractive fee of 34 billion rupees valid for 15 years, Reliance said.
It said Gujarat, one of India's richest states, has about 800,000 telephone lines and a waiting list of more than 184,000 lines.
"Reliance Telecom will install approximately 50,000 lines in the first year, 150,000 lines in the second year and 300,000 lines in the third year," the statement said.
It planned to install a million lines by the end of the fifth year. Its services will start by the end of this year in Baroda, Ahmedabad, Surat, Jamnagar and Rajkot, the firm said.
Reliance Group has also obtained licenses to build and operate cellular services in seven regions covering 13 states.
It said the group was poised to emerge as the country's largest player in telecommunication services.
